summary: Federal Communications Commission urges preservation of E-Rate program to ensure broadband connectivity for schools and libraries, citing cost savings and budget constraints. The school district urges the FCC to preserve E-Rate, emphasizing its role in providing essential connectivity for students and libraries. The district argues that the program is crucial for modern education and economic preparedness. The superintendent calls for rejecting proposals to sunset or eliminate E-Rate and instead works to strengthen and modernize the program.

claims.argument: E-Rate has enabled schools to build necessary infrastructure
claims.evidence_quote: E-Rate has enabled schools (public and private) and libraries to build and maintain the connectivity necessary for students and patrons to participate fully in modern education. As our nation seeks to prepare students for college, careers, and an increasingly technology-driven economy, now is not the time to undermine the very program and related infrastructure that makes those opportunities possible.
